title.narrative: Provision of essential education, nutrition, and child protection services for conflict affected internally displaced persons and host communities in Syria.

description.narrative: The project addresses urgent education, nutrition, and child protection needs of displaced populations and host communities affected escalating conflict across Syria. Over six months, with a budget of USD 4,166,565, it aims to mitigate impacts of the crisis on children and families by providing essential services that save lives and reduce vulnerabilities. A total of 405,693 people will be reached (30,000 women, 187,554 girls, 7,943 men, 180,196 boys), including people with disabilities, across 12 Governorates (Aleppo, Ar-Raqqa, Damascus, Dar’a, Deir-ez-Zor, Hama, Homs, Idleb, Lattakia, Rural Damascus and Tartous), with a focus on internally displaced persons (IDPs) and those in host communities.Education: The project ensures continuity of learning by:Providing maintenance of the existing prefabricated classrooms to increase school capacity to host more children in a safe and inclusive learning environment.Providing non-formal education to support children at-risk of dropping out to continue learningDistributing education supplies including textbooks, stationary kits, and school kits to address shortage in learning materials.Enhancing capacity of teachers on psycho-social and violence mitigation skills.367,750 children (187,553 girls, 180,198 boys) and 1,090 teachers (708 women, 382 men) will be directly reached, including IDPs, returnees and host communities.Nutrition: The project focuses on preventative services for children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLW), including nutrition screening, provision of preventive supplies and skilled counselling on IYCF-E. 80,000 children and women (30,000 women, 25,000 girls, 25,000 boys), including host communities, IDP, and returnees, will gain access to quality nutrition services via mobile teams in the targeted Governorates, especially in camps. Child Protection: The project focuses on safeguarding children from violence, abuse and exploitation, whilst promoting psychosocial wellbeing through: Case management services, including family tracing, reunification and alternative care.Mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) and Psychological First Aid (PFA) in safe spaces, helping children and caregivers to manage distress.Outreach campaigns on child protection, mine risk education, gender-based violence (GBV) risks, and harmful practices, such as child marriage.35,300 people (7,943 women, 9,707 girls, 7,943 men, 9,707 boys) including displaced people and host communities affected by the conflict in Syria, will be reached via mobile and static teams, child friendly spaces and community centers.Strong partnerships with NGOs and government entities, including the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs, will ensure community-driven, culturally sensitive interventions. By leveraging community structures and ongoing programming, the project addresses urgent needs of displaced populations while reducing vulnerabilities in host communities. UNICEF’s six field offices and partner network will ensure access, assess regional dynamics, and adapt responses to evolving needs.
